definitions.full: H6118. eqeb עֵ֫קֶב noun [masculine] consequence , usually as adverb accusative as a consequence of, because (that) also reward, end (see below עָקַב ; and cf, heel figurative consequence, result); — 1 Isa 5:23 שֹׁחַד עֵקֶב רָשָׁע מַצְדִּיקֵי (adverb accusative) in consequence of a bribe. Psa 40:16 (= 70:4 ) בָּשְׁתָּם עֵקֶב על (pleon.) according to the consequence of their shame, i.e. in consequence of the disgrace falling upon them. Hence as conjunction אֲשֶׁר עֵקֶב as a consequence of (the fact) that, because , Gen 22:18 ע ׳בְּקֹלִי שָׁמַעְתָּ אֲשֶׁר 26:5 ; 2Sam 12:6 ; so כִּי עֵקֶב 12:10 ; Amos 4:12 ׳ע לך אעשׂה זאת כִּי ; עֵקֶב alone, Num 14:24 , and (followed by imperfect) Deut 7:12 ׳ע תשׁמעון in consequence of your hearkening, etc., 8:20 . 2 consequence = gain, reward , Psa 19:12 רָב עֵקֶב בְּשָׁמְרָם , Prov 22:4 י (וְ)יִרְאַת עֲנָוָה ׳עֵקֶב וגו ׳עשֶׁר . 3 end (of time), adverb accusative, Psa 119:33 ע ׳וְאֶצֳּרֶנָּה to the end , 119:112 ׳ע לְעוֺלָם (compare Ecclus 16:3; עִקְבָּא ᵑ7 (rare)).
